exit: 0
--- stdout
keywords:
  sequence derived_from none param in out block true false Real Integer Boolean

types:
  Real Integer Boolean

tags:
  @unit @quantity @displayUnit @brick @s223 @qudt @haystack @name @label @provisional

base units:
  m kg s A K mol cd rad sr Hz N Pa J W C V F Ohm S Wb T H lm lx Bq Gy Sv kat

scale factors (time only; one symbol is exactly this many base units; alone as a unit suffix on a parameter declared in the base unit, it scales the number, rounding once):
  min  60 s
  h    3600 s
  d    86400 s

parse codes (text form, exit 2):
  not-utf8              the input is not UTF-8
  byte-order-mark       the input starts with a byte-order mark
  control-character     a tab, carriage return, other control character or bidirectional override
  input-too-large       the input is larger than 4 MiB
  too-many-lines        the input has more than 100,000 lines
  line-too-long         a line is longer than 8,192 bytes
  token-too-long        a name, number, suffix, atom or provenance id is longer than 256 bytes
  string-too-long       a string is longer than 4,096 bytes as written
  comment-too-long      a comment is longer than 8,189 bytes after its #
  nesting-too-deep      lists nest deeper than 2
  too-many-statements   more than 65,536 statements of one kind or assignments in one block
  unterminated-string   a string has no closing quote on its line
  bad-escape            a backslash escape other than \", \\ or \n
  malformed-number      a number with a leading + or zero, a bare dot, an empty exponent or glued letters
  integer-out-of-range  an integer outside the 64-bit signed range
  non-finite-number     NaN, inf or Infinity as a value, or a real that overflows binary64
  malformed-suffix      a unit suffix that is not a unit expression
  unit-not-base         a unit suffix that is neither built from base SI units nor one of the scaled symbols min, h and d alone
  malformed-atom        a tag atom or provenance id with a byte outside printable ASCII
  stray-token           a token where the grammar allows none, or a missing one
  unknown-keyword       a line that starts with no statement keyword and is not a connection
  unknown-tag           a boundary tag the grammar does not name
  duplicate-tag         a boundary tag other than @haystack written twice on one statement
  unknown-type          a type other than Real, Integer or Boolean
  missing-sequence      the file does not start with a sequence statement
  missing-derived-from  the sequence statement is not followed by a derived_from statement
  misplaced-statement   a second sequence or derived_from statement
  misplaced-value       a reference or a list as a sequence parameter's value
  malformed-list        an empty, ragged or mixed list
  unclosed-bracket      a ( or [ that is never closed
  comment-before-close  a comment after the last item of a (...) or [...]

finding codes, stage 1 (exit 1):
  empty-sequence               the sequence has no blocks
  invalid-name                 a declared name is not an identifier, or is a reserved word or keyword
  duplicate-name               a name is declared twice across parameters, inputs, outputs and blocks
  class-not-found              a block's class path is not a registered class
  class-not-authorable         a block's class is an engine-reserved lowering identity
  unknown-parameter            an assignment names no parameter of the block's class
  parameter-not-settable       an assignment names a parameter no author may set
  duplicate-parameter          a block assigns one parameter twice
  missing-required-parameter   a required parameter is not assigned
  parameter-kind-mismatch      a value's kind does not fit the parameter
  parameter-out-of-range       a value breaks a catalog rule, widths included
  non-finite-parameter         a Real value is NaN or infinite
  unit-suffix-mismatch         a unit suffix that is not the parameter's declared unit, a scaled one where none is declared, or one that disagrees with its value
  unknown-enum-literal         an enumeration member is not a member of the parameter's type
  unknown-enum-type            a sequence parameter's type names no enumeration, or names a constant package
  unknown-parameter-reference  a reference names no sequence parameter
  malformed-connection         a connection endpoint is not name or block.port
  unknown-source               a connection source is neither a boundary input nor a block output
  unknown-target               a connection target is neither a boundary output nor a block input
  unknown-port                 a connection names a port the configured block does not have on that side
  invalid-semantic-point       a semantic, quantity or displayUnit field is malformed
  invalid-bound                a boundary bound the boundary's type cannot take
  non-finite-bound             a boundary bound is NaN or infinite
  crossed-bounds               a boundary's min exceeds its max
  invalid-provenance-id        the derived_from provenance id is malformed
  single-assignment            two connections drive one block input or boundary output

finding codes, stage 2 (exit 1; engine codes pass through as well):
  document-too-large  the emitted document is larger than the engine loads
  load-failed         the throwaway engine refused the emitted document

wire codes (exit 2):
  not-utf8              the bytes are not UTF-8
  byte-order-mark       the document starts with a byte-order mark
  input-too-large       the document is larger than 4 MiB
  nesting-too-deep      objects and arrays nest deeper than 8 levels
  list-too-long         a list has more than 65,536 entries
  string-too-long       a string is longer than 4,096 bytes
  duplicate-key         an object repeats a key
  non-finite-number     NaN or Infinity as a number, or a real that overflows binary64
  integer-out-of-range  an integer token outside the 64-bit signed range
  control-character     a string carries a control character
  unknown-key           an object carries a key its schema does not define
  missing-key           an object lacks a required key
  wrong-type            a value has the wrong JSON type or an unknown enumerator
  json-syntax           the document is not JSON
  bound-list-too-long   a boundary's min or max list has more than one number
  malformed-connection  a connection is not `source -> target` with exactly one ->

import codes (import, exit 2):
  too-large                 the document is over the importer's size limit (the tool's bounded read refuses an over-size input first, as input-too-large)
  not-strict-json           the bytes are not UTF-8 or not JSON, nesting is deeper than 128 levels, an object repeats a key, or an integer is outside the 64-bit signed range
  limit-exceeded            v0 graph JSON: nesting, a list or a string over a read bound
  unknown-key               a property, top-level key or @context term the flat CXF subset does not define
  namespace-mismatch        the @context binds the S231 vocabulary in a namespace the engine does not read
  missing-key               a required key is absent: a node without @id, a parameter without a type or a value
  wrong-shape               a value of the wrong JSON shape: a relation that is not references, a label or term that is not a string
  no-root                   no node contains blocks
  duplicate-id              a node @id is declared twice
  unresolved-reference      a reference to no node, or to a node outside the root's IRI
  stray-node                a node no root relation reaches, or one reached twice
  invalid-name              a root @id or local name that breaks the identifier syntax, or a path deeper than block.member
  nested-composite          a second node that contains blocks (outside the subset)
  instance-member           hasInstance (outside the subset)
  constant-member           hasConstant (outside the subset)
  conditional-component     a conditional component (outside the subset)
  array-connector           an array boundary or port (outside the subset)
  array-sequence-parameter  an array sequence parameter (outside the subset)
  expression-value          a value that is an expression, or a name that is no sequence parameter (outside the subset)
  port-attribute            unit, quantity, displayUnit, min, max or nominal on a block port (not authorable)
  connector-attribute       nominal or unbounded on a boundary (not carried)
  two-spellings             one property written under two spellings on one node (S231:unit beside qudt:hasUnit)
  driving-sink              a boundary output or a block input drives a connection
  class-outside-obc         a block class outside Buildings.Controls.OBC
  datatype-mismatch         a value, bound or connector that disagrees with its declared type
  unknown-datatype          a declared type that is no supported scalar and no named type
  unknown-member-type       a member path whose enumeration or constant package the engine does not know
  malformed-literal         a non-finite or unparsable number, an unknown XSD datatype or a bad string escape
  array-shape               an array's sizes, rank or catalog template disagree with its value
  string-value              v0 graph JSON: a string parameter value
  malformed-connection      v0 graph JSON: a connection that is not `source -> target` with exactly one ->

error codes (exit 2):
  missing-from              stdin (-) was given without --from
  unknown-form              the name ends in neither .oce nor .json (for id and diff, nor .jsonld or .cxf.json) and --from was not given
  not-found                 the input path does not exist
  not-a-file                the input path is a directory or another non-file
  read-failed               the input could not be read
  input-too-large           the input is over its limit (4 MiB a sequence, vector, commissioning spec or mapping file, 8 MiB CXF, 1 GiB a trend source); refused before it is read
  invalid-namespace         --namespace is empty, too long, not printable ASCII or does not end in #, / or :
  unspellable               the model cannot be written as text, or (import --wire) in the wire form so that it reads back
  write-failed              the output could not be written or renamed into place, or (verify --out) DIR is not an existing directory, or (verify --commission --out) DIR/outputs or a regular DIR/receipt.json already exists
  write-needs-file          --write or -o cannot rewrite stdin
  write-needs-text          fmt --write rewrites text files only; redirect a wire file's text instead
  malformed-param           a --param is not NAME=VALUE
  unknown-param             a --param names no parameter of the class
  duplicate-param           a --param names one parameter twice
  malformed-value           a --param value is not of the parameter's type
  ports-unresolvable        the facade could not name the ports of an accepted table
  emit-refused              the emitter refused for a reason this tool does not know
  unknown-subject-form      a verify subject is not .jsonld, .cxf.json, .oce or .json and --subject-form was not given
  mutant-outside-directory  a mutant path resolves, through a link or a drive prefix, outside the vector file's directory
  reference-required        verify --commission: the spec has several references and --reference was not given; the detail lists each
  file-outside-directory    verify --commission: a CXF, mapping or trend source path resolves, through a link or a drive prefix, outside the spec's directory
  namespace-needs-authored  id --namespace was given beside a CXF document; only a text or wire file is emitted
  not-loadable              id or a CXF side of diff: the engine refused the document; id: or the sequence has error findings; there is no content id or diff
  no-content-id             the facade could not name a model it loaded
  output-form-mismatch      import -o or emit -o names a file whose name reads as another form than the one written (.oce text, .json wire, .jsonld and .cxf.json CXF)
  output-is-input           emit -o or import -o is the input file itself (another spelling of its path, the file an input link names, or on Unix a hard link to it), or, on Unix, the regular file standard input reads; or verify --out DIR (vector or --commission) would write DIR/receipt.json over a file the run reads, by path, through a link or as a hard link; nothing is written
  output-not-a-file         the path a verb would write (emit -o, import -o, fmt --write's file, verify --out's DIR/receipt.json) is a symbolic link, dangling or not, a directory, a named pipe, a socket or a device; oce never writes through a link (give the path of the file it names); nothing is read or written
  mixed-forms               diff: the two names read as two forms (text, wire, CXF) and --from was not given; both sides are one form
  stdin-twice               diff: both sides are stdin (-), which is read once

bind and run codes (verify, exit 2):
  subject-load-failed           the engine refused the subject, or a text or wire subject has an error finding
  unknown-input                 an input name matches no boundary input
  ambiguous-input               an input suffix matches several boundary inputs (candidates)
  duplicate-input               two input names of one scenario resolve to one boundary input
  input-not-supplied            a scenario supplies no value for a boundary input

  ambiguous-output              an output suffix matches several boundary outputs (candidates)

  param-path-duplicate          two keys of one params map name one parameter

  value-type-mismatch           a value its port's or parameter's type does not take
  value-not-representable       a number no binary64 holds exactly where a Real is read
  enum-port-unsupported         the subject has an Enum boundary input or output
  unsupported-port-type         the subject has a String boundary input or output
  too-many-frames               the run would execute more than 16,777,216 frames, or one scenario more than replay allows

  too-many-frame-bytes          the run's frames weighted by document bytes would pass 2^40
  mutant-missing                a listed mutant was given no bytes

  too-many-mutant-bytes         the mutants are larger than 64 MiB together; refused before any is read

  mutant-boundary-differs       a mutant's input or output paths or types are not the subject's (path)
  mutant-identical              a mutant has the subject's content id
  mutant-param-refused          a mutant refuses an edit the subject admits (cause)
  run-refused                   the engine refused a frame for a reason about the run, not the frame
  compare-refused               the envelope gave a tolerance window or a commissioning output no result (cause: reference-outside-envelope, work-limit-exceeded, ...)
  replay-failed                 the replay stopped with an error (cause: trace-too-large, engine-setup, ...)
  window-uncovered              a window held no executed tick after a run with no refused frame
  reference-out-of-range        the commissioning spec has no reference at the index asked for
  reference-incomplete          the commissioning reference has no cxf or no window, which a run needs
  spec-refused                  an outputs or indicators key matches no output, several, or disagrees with another (cause)
  unknown-indicator             an indicator name is no signal of the sequence and no indicatorSources point
  indicator-not-boolean         an indicator sample is not Boolean and not exactly 0 or 1
  duplicate-output              two mapped names of the expected outputs resolve to one boundary output
  frame-refused                 the engine refused a trend frame (cause: its class); no receipt
  too-many-sources              the commissioning reference reads more than 256 trend sources
  too-many-outputs              the commissioning reference compares more than 4,096 outputs
  source-refused                a trend source or the point mapping was refused (cause: the source reader's code)
  unit-refused                  a mapped point's unit does not fit its sequence port (cause: the unit code)
  too-many-indicators           the commissioning reference's indicator rules name more than 64 indicators

  not-utf8              the spec is not UTF-8

  non-finite-number     NaN or Infinity as a number, or a real that overflows binary64
  integer-out-of-range  an integer outside 64 bits, or one read as a real above 2^53

  unknown-schema        schema is not oce/commissioning-spec/v1
  too-many-parameters   a reference's parameters map has more than 256 entries
  too-many-keys         an outputs, indicators or columns map has more than 4,096 keys

  invalid-time-origin   time.origin is not an RFC 3339 instant with an explicit offset

  invalid-sampling      a sampling is not above zero
  invalid-window        a window's start is after its stop

  unmatched-key         the cause of spec-refused: an outputs or indicators key selects no output of the sequence

  conflicting-override  the cause of spec-refused: two outputs keys of one kind give one output one tolerance field two values
  work-limit-exceeded   the cause of spec-refused: matching the keys against the outputs needs more than 2^28 work units

unit codes (verify --commission, the cause of unit-refused, exit 2):
  unknown-pair             units/v1 lists no conversion from the device's unit to the CDL point's
  one-sided                one side of a mapped point has a unit and the other none
  empty-unit               a unit is written as the empty string
  overflow                 a finite reading's conversion is beyond the largest binary64
  absolute-for-difference  an absolute temperature pair on a TemperatureDifference port
  difference-for-absolute  a temperature difference pair on a ThermodynamicTemperature port
  port-unit-mismatch       the mapping's cdl.unit is not the unit the sequence port declares

frame refusal classes (verify --commission, the cause of frame-refused, exit 2):
  input-type                  an input value of the wrong type for its port
  input-non-finite            an infinite input value
  input-domain                an input value outside its port's declared bounds (a wrong unit or mapping, most often)
  non-finite-time             a frame time that is not finite
  time-out-of-range           a frame time beyond the engine's magnitude limit
  time-regression             a frame time earlier than the one before
  non-finite-time-step        a time step that is not finite
  model-time-unrepresentable  a model time the engine cannot represent
  run                         a refusal about the engine or the run, not the frame (run-refused carries it)

diff codes (diff, exit 2):
  outside-root        a CXF block or boundary is not named under its document's root (one the engine exported included); at names the side
  unresolved-ports    the ports of a CXF block cannot be named from its class and ground parameters (never expected for a loaded document)
  unreadable-blob     the facade reads no summary from a blob (the blob comparison; diff reads no blob)
  unexpected-refusal  the facade refused a blob with an error that is not a blob refusal (never expected; diff reads no blob)

exit codes:
  0  yes: clean, canonical, resolved, every scenario or compared output passed, an id printed, a document imported, nothing differs
  1  no: an error finding, a non-canonical file, ports that do not resolve, a failed or no_data verdict, any difference (diff)
  2  error: a usage, read, parse, size or I/O failure, a run with no verdict, an input with no content id (id), a document the importer refuses or the output form cannot spell (import), or a side that does not load or cannot be named (diff); the question was not answered
